_comment: The version each device runs, and what an update is allowed to replace on it. This file - not the release list - is what devices read. Publishing a release does not roll it out; editing this file does. Moving a version back rolls that fleet back on its next check. See ADMIN_MANUAL.md section 8b.
_format_version: The version to install, or "" for none yet. Devices upgrade OR downgrade to reach it. A device with PIN set in its own config/update.conf ignores this.
_format_paths: exclude: paths this hardware keeps, on top of whatever the release already protects. include: extra paths this hardware takes, on top of what the release ships - and the one way to claim a path the updater's deny-list normally protects, such as an audio folder. A release can never do that; this file can, because it is edited by hand and not shipped in a public archive. Forced paths are logged as FORCED: on the device and are never rsynced with --delete. var/update/ and var/installed_version stay refused - the updater is writing to them while it runs. Both lists are additions to the release's own, never a replacement. Paths are relative to ~/Desktop/scheduler/ and a trailing slash means a directory. See ADMIN_MANUAL.md section 8b.
_format_stale: include and exclude are keyed by hardware, not by version: whatever is listed keeps applying to every release that follows. Take an entry out when the rollout it was added for is superseded - nothing will remind you.
_format_shorthand: A variant with no path rules can be written as just the version string: "zero": "1.0.3".
